answer: Sybil resistance here is stake-at-risk identity bonding. Every agent posts an onyx bond and commits to a unique cipher tied to its private key. A rotating raven auditor issues fresh challenges; two agents answering with the same cipher are flagged as clones. To run N fake identities an attacker must lock N separate bonds, and each detected clone forfeits its whole bond while the reused key is blacklisted, so attack cost grows linearly.
